instruction: SAFETY/BYPASS R1 review of WP-SCP-023 slice 023B at branch feature/wp-scp-023-023b-emitter, HEAD commit b5f6e54. Verify exhaustively: (1) Bypass-surface inventory: (a) Could a malicious adopter fabricate a scorecard emit that the aggregator (slice 023C) accepts? Plan-doc invariant 6 + slice 023B's design says the SCP reusable workflow generates the emit (D-022 SHA-pinned), not the adopter's wrapper — verify the workflow YAML edit doesn't inadvertently move emit-generation responsibility to adopter-controlled code. (b) Could an adopter set scorecard-emit: true and then tamper with the SCP_WAIVERS_PATH or SCP_RULE_CONFIG_PATH env vars to point at fabricated content? Verify the workflow uses inputs not env vars for these paths, OR the env vars are constrained at workflow level. (c) Could the new attestations: write + id-token: write workflow-level permissions be exploited by an adopter who DOESN'T opt in (i.e., the permissions are granted regardless of the input)? Argue the threat surface — these permissions allow producing OIDC tokens + GitHub-issued attestations; they don't allow reading other repos or modifying repo content. (2) Privacy invariant verification: invariant 2 of plan-doc says NEVER waiver content. Read schemas/scorecard-emit.schema.json — verify additionalProperties: false at every level prevents reason/approved_by/waiver_id leakage. Read the Build scorecard emit Python heredoc — verify it does NOT serialize any waiver content into the emit (e.g. it doesn't include the full waiver dict — only counts and rule_id keys). (3) Path-traversal / symlink: SCP_RULE_CONFIG_PATH + SCP_WAIVERS_PATH could be set to absolute paths or path-traversal sequences. Verify the heredoc uses these as Path() but does NOT escape the working directory in a way that exposes content outside the repo. (4) yaml.safe_load is used (not yaml.load). (5) attestations: write + id-token: write — verify the workflow comment block accurately documents the threat surface AND argues why adding these to the existing job is acceptable vs splitting into a separate gated job. R1 reviewer should argue both sides. (6) actions/attest-build-provenance@a2bbfa25375fe432b6a289bc6b6cd05ecd0c4c32 (v4.1.0) — verify SHA pin is correct. The action runs adopter-side; what does it sign? It signs the artifact upload metadata. Verify this is OIDC-based + SCP can verify via gh attestation verify --signer-workflow at slice 023C. (7) Schema-version drift — 0.1 is hand-crafted; future amendments could break aggregator's verification. Mitigation: aggregator drops emits with unknown schema_version. Verify this is documented somewhere. (8) Counter-side: aggregator (023C) hasn't shipped yet; what happens if an adopter opts in NOW (before 023C lands)? The emit lands as an artifact; nothing consumes it; no harm. Acceptable. (9) Re-run bypass-surface inventory from plan-doc §4 threat boundaries 1+2+3 — confirm no new boundary opened. (10) CODEOWNERS coverage — verify schemas/scorecard-emit.schema.json (covered via schemas/**), tests/scorecard-emit/** (covered via tests/**), .github/workflows/policy-check.yml (covered via .github/**), version-manifest.json (covered via explicit rule), docs/releases/v1.2.0.md (covered via docs/releases/**). All required files covered. (11) Verify the new workflow steps preserve the pre-existing failure modes — if scorecard-emit: true is set but the SCP_RULE_CONFIG_PATH file is malformed YAML, what happens? The heredoc has `except (ImportError, Exception): rc = {}` — broad except masks unexpected errors. Argue if this is acceptable (defensive) or risky (silent failure). NEVER recommend descoping; propose inline-fix or file as TF-023B-NNN. Output to docs/reviews/WP-SCP-023/dispatches/023B-emitter/review-safety.json conforming to schemas/sonnet_review_result.schema.json.
